# 4 Maccabees Chapter 14 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Mother's Reason Over Maternal Love

---

**14:1** Even more wonderful: how they urged one another toward death by their words of encouragement to one another.

**14:2** For it was reason that had made them firm in their convictions, and the law had made them noble, and their love of one another had drawn them forward.

**14:3** For seeing how much they suffered and how they held firm, even the tyrant and his guards were moved with wonder.

**14:4** Indeed, even the parents who had raised such children did not grieve at their deaths but rejoiced in their courage.

**14:5** Even the mothers who had nursed these brothers were not overcome with grief at their deaths.

**14:6** For all the women who are devoted to virtue are strengthened by reason, even as the mother of these seven was strengthened.

**14:7** When she saw them being tortured one by one, her love for her children did not weaken her will to see them die for the law.

**14:8** But instead she watched as each of them died and considered this a sight worthy of the greatest joy.

**14:9** For she herself loved the law more than she loved her children.

**14:10** Her children were noble and obedient, and therefore she urged them on to the struggle.

**14:11** What was the source of such love for the law in this woman? It was her piety toward God.

**14:12** For the reason that is devoted to God is able to overcome even maternal affection when the service of God demands it.

**14:13** Let no one therefore suppose that a woman is weaker in character or in virtue. For a woman who has been educated in the law proves to be in no way weaker than men.

**14:14** Rather, if we are to speak truly, she proves to be stronger — for she was not herself undergoing torture, but she was watching seven sons tortured and she endured it all.

**14:15** For when reason, through devotion to God, has taken charge of the passions, it governs even maternal affection for children.

**14:16** And surely, just as the wise Abraham was willing to offer his son Isaac on the altar for the sake of God, and the hand of the father was not moved by compassion for the child so as to stay the knife,

**14:17** so too this mother, moved by no such compulsion but by her own will, sacrificed her seven sons for the sake of God.

**14:18** With her reason she governed her passions, and she overcame the pain of losing seven sons.

**14:19** She proved by her faithfulness to God that reason is indeed sovereign over the passions, even over the most powerful of them.

**14:20** Therefore she is greater than all the noble athletes — for she wrestled against passion in the most intimate of arenas, the arena of a mother's heart.

**14:21** How fitting then that she should receive the crown of victory, the crown of imperishable life, for having overcome every passion through reason!
